It summarizes five signs—heart rate, breathing effort, muscle tone, reflex response, and color—into a score from 0 to 10, with lower scores indicating greater need for medical attention.

Type: cognitive or neuropsychological test result. Description: 'Coding test result' refers to the score or outcome of a coding task, usually a timed assessment in which a person matches symbols, numbers, or patterns according to a key. It is commonly used to measure processing speed, attention, visual-motor coordination, and short-term working efficiency in clinical or psychological testing.

Type: neuropsychological test result. Description: 'Kohs block design test result' refers to the score or performance outcome on the Kohs Block Design Test, a cognitive assessment in which a person recreates patterns using colored blocks. The test is used to evaluate visuospatial ability, nonverbal reasoning, problem-solving, and perceptual organization.

Type: demographic / socioeconomic variable. Description: 'Baseline maternal occupation' refers to the mother’s job or occupational role at the start of a study, assessment, or intervention. It is used as a background characteristic that may reflect socioeconomic position, work-related exposures, and social context relevant to maternal or child health outcomes.

Type: demographic / socioeconomic variable. Description: 'Baseline parental education' refers to the education level attained by one or both parents at the start of a study, assessment, or intervention. It is usually recorded as the highest grade completed, degree earned, or years of schooling, and is used as an indicator of family socioeconomic and educational background.

Type: demographic / social status variable. Description: 'Baseline marital status' refers to a person’s relationship status at the start of a study, assessment, or intervention. It typically categorizes whether the person is married, single, divorced, separated, widowed, or partnered, and is used as a background social characteristic that may influence health and life outcomes.

Type: neonatal assessment / clinical measurement. Description: 'Birth measurement' refers to the physical measurements recorded for a newborn at or shortly after birth. These commonly include birth weight, length, head circumference, and sometimes chest circumference, and are used to assess the infant’s size, growth status, and overall neonatal health.

Type: mental process / cognitive function. Description: 'Spatial imagery' refers to the mental representation and manipulation of spatial relationships, such as the position, orientation, size, or movement of objects in space. It is an important cognitive ability involved in navigation, visualizing patterns, and solving visuospatial problems.

Type: educational / cognitive performance measure. Description: 'Spelling performance' refers to how accurately and effectively a person spells words on a test or task. It is used to assess written language skills, including orthographic knowledge, phonological processing, memory for word forms, and academic achievement.

Type: pregnancy / fetal age measure. Description: 'Gestational age' refers to how far a pregnancy has progressed, usually measured in weeks from the first day of the pregnant person’s last menstrual period. It is used to assess fetal development, estimate the due date, and classify births as preterm, term, or post-term.

Type: clinical assessment / neurologic status variable. Description: 'Baseline neurological status' refers to a person’s usual or initial level of neurologic functioning at the start of a study, evaluation, or treatment period. It may include consciousness, motor and sensory function, reflexes, coordination, speech, and cognition, and serves as a reference point for detecting later neurologic change.

Type: demographic / family composition variable. Description: 'Baseline only child status' refers to whether the participant or index child has no siblings at the start of a study or assessment. It is used to describe family structure and household context, which may be relevant to developmental, social, behavioral, or health-related analyses.

Type: neonatal clinical assessment score. Description: 'Apgar score' is a quick assessment of a newborn’s condition performed shortly after birth, typically at 1 and 5 minutes. It rates five signs—heart rate, breathing effort, muscle tone, reflex response, and skin color—on a scale that totals 0 to 10, helping clinicians judge how well the baby is adapting after delivery.

Type: population group / demographic characteristic. Description: 'Ethnicity' refers to a person’s identification with a social or cultural group that shares common heritage, history, traditions, language, or origin. In clinical and research settings, it is used as a demographic variable because it can be associated with social experiences, health patterns, and differences in disease risk or care.

Type: educational / cognitive test score. Description: 'Reading quotient' refers to a score used to quantify reading ability relative to age or expected level of performance. It is typically derived from standardized reading assessments and is used to evaluate reading development, achievement, or possible reading difficulties.

Type: neonatal growth / clinical attribute. Description: 'Birth weight for gestational age' refers to a newborn’s weight interpreted in relation to how many weeks of pregnancy had been completed at birth. It is used to classify infants as small, appropriate, or large for gestational age and helps assess fetal growth and neonatal health.

Type: research assessment / knowledge variable. Description: 'Baseline trial arm knowledge' refers to a participant’s understanding at the start of a study about the treatment group, intervention group, or comparison group in a clinical trial. It is used to assess initial awareness or comprehension of trial assignment or study design before further intervention or follow-up.
